record.original_question: How do recurrences in a dynamical system, including periodic orbits and more general recurrent structures either near the hole or elsewhere in phase space, affect escape for systems with little or no hyperbolicity?

evidence.quote: One feature that is common to all classes of billiards, classical and quantum is the role of periodic orbits in the open problem.

Open problem 18. Recurrence: Give a general description of how the escape problem is affected by recurrences in the system (periodic orbits or more general), in the vicinity of the hole and/or elsewhere, for systems with little or no hyperbolicity.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M, T, \mu)$ be a measure-preserving dynamical system on a phase space $M$ with an invariant probability measure $\mu$, and let $H \subset M$ be a measurable subset (the "hole"). Define the survival set up to time $n$ by
$$S_n(H) = \{x \in M : T^k(x) \notin H \text{ for all } 0 \le k \le n\},$$
and define the escape rate (when the limit exists) by
$$\gamma(H) = -\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{n} \log \mu(S_n(H)).$$
For systems $(M,T,\mu)$ that exhibit little or no hyperbolicity (for example, parabolic, intermittent, or mixed-phase-space systems with elliptic islands, zero or weak Lyapunov exponents, or polynomial mixing), give a general quantitative description of how $\gamma(H)$ and the finer asymptotics of $\mu(S_n(H))$ are affected by recurrent structures of $T$. In particular, characterize the contribution to escape of:
(a) periodic orbits intersecting or close to the boundary of $H$;
(b) periodic orbits and more general recurrent invariant sets (e.g. KAM tori, almost-invariant sets, neutral fixed points) located elsewhere in $M$;
(c) the interplay between such recurrence and the geometry/location of $H$,
and obtain a unifying formula or correction principle (analogous to the hyperbolic escape-rate formulas involving sums over periodic orbits) that applies in the non-hyperbolic regime.
artifact.category_tag: open dynamical systems and escape rates
artifact.status_search_result: The web search reveals active research on escape rates and periodic orbits, including periodic-orbit formulas in chaotic (hyperbolic) settings and case studies of escape in Hamiltonian and almost-periodic systems, but no general theory describing the influence of recurrent structures on escape for systems with little or no hyperbolicity. The problem appears to remain open, with only partial progress in specific model classes.

status_evidence.title: Periodic Orbits and Escapes in Dynamical Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Studies periodic orbits and escape in specific Hamiltonian systems; treats particular examples rather than a general non-hyperbolic theory.
status_evidence.claim: Work on periodic orbits and escape exists but is restricted to particular models, not a general framework.

status_evidence.title: Computing Classical Escape Rates from Periodic Orbits in Chaotic Hydrogen
status_evidence.snippet: Periodic-orbit theory used to compute escape rates in chaotic (hyperbolic) systems.
status_evidence.claim: Periodic-orbit escape-rate formulas are well developed in hyperbolic regimes, but the non-hyperbolic case is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Escaping Orbits Are also Rare in the Almost Periodic Fermi–Ulam Ping-Pong
status_evidence.snippet: Shows escaping orbits have measure zero in a specific non-hyperbolic model.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial, model-specific results are available for escape in weakly/non-hyperbolic systems.
